selection: Eight runtime bug-fix PRs merged after the prior Zod runtime holdout. Each has a public executable reproduction and a distinct green control. No fixing diff was opened before this file was frozen.

cases.issue: A pipe hands its output schema the caller's issues array. catch and optional wrappers can then treat someone else's issue as their own, substitute for it, and clear a strict-object violation. A wrapper's inner schema should run on its own payload.
An enum with no values compiles to an empty alternation and incorrectly matches the empty string. Empty enums and literals should match nothing.
fromJSONSchema maps RFC 3339 format time to a partial local time. It should accept seconds with Z or a numeric offset and reject a local time without an offset.
RFC 3339 date-time requires seconds when a Z or numeric offset is present. z.iso.datetime should reject minute-precision Z input while continuing to accept seconds-qualified input.

z.number().multipleOf(0.07) rejects exact decimal multiples such as 2.03 and 4.06 because quotient rounding exceeds a one-ULP tolerance. Exact multiples should pass while nearby non-multiples remain rejected.

A catch callback after coercion receives the intermediate parsed value instead of the original input. ctx.value should expose the input passed to parse so a fallback can distinguish string and numeric inputs.

The JSON Schema pattern for string includes with position N allows exactly N leading characters, but String.includes treats N as a minimum start offset. The emitted pattern should accept a match at position N or later.
cases.target: import * as z from "../packages/zod/src/v4/index.ts";const s=z.string().includes("foo",{position:2});const pattern=(z.toJSONSchema(s) as any).pattern;const re=new RegExp(pattern);console.log(s.safeParse("xxxfoo").success&&re.test("xxxfoo"));
cases.control: import * as z from "../packages/zod/src/v4/index.ts";const s=z.string().includes("foo",{position:2});const re=new RegExp((z.toJSONSchema(s) as any).pattern);console.log(s.safeParse("xxfoo").success&&re.test("xxfoo"));

cases.issue: Adding catch to a chain containing prefault and optional can make a previously successful undefined parse fail. catch should only turn failure into success and must not resurrect an issue optional already resolved.
A memoized shared node reuses live issue objects, so a second visitor prefixes onto the first visitor's path. Each reference should receive an independent issue with its own left or right path.
cases.target: import * as z from "../packages/zod/src/v4/index.ts";z.config({jitless:true});const Node:any=z.object({name:z.string(),get left(){return z.optional(Node);},get right(){return z.optional(Node);}});const shared:any={name:123};const r=Node.safeParse({name:"root",left:shared,right:shared});const paths=!r.success?r.error.issues.map((i:any)=>i.path.join(".")).sort():[];console.log(paths.join(",")==="left.name,right.name");
